questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose Sorbonne because I wanted to go on exchange to a university with a high academic level, and I wanted to go to an interesting country with the opportunity to learn a new language.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The academic level at Sorbonne was sometimes high and sometimes not so much.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very difficult. None of the information is sent out, and often there was not a person or office you could go to to figure things out. Extremely frustrating experience. Moreover, there is a lot of things which you dont know that you dont know, and noone is helping you with it.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: None. A welcome event was held 1 or 2 weeks after the start of the semester. Ironically, half of the event was held in french. Registering for courses is not centralized, so you have to the one person in the whole university responsible for signing people up for the given course. Meaning if you take 5 courses, which is normal, you have to find the 5 individuals that can sign you up for each course. How do you find them? Luck, guess, and asking around, the information often doesnt exist in writing.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I had a great semester abroad, but it was all in spite of the universitys best efforts, because as an exchange student, especially if you are not fluent in french, feels deliberately impossible.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: No idea, I applied to the danish house at the cite international universitare paris, and got a room. I highly recommend this.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Public transport closes at night, but Uber and Bolt are incredibly cheap.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Practically impossible, I still dont quite understand how I managed to find a way through it.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Courses are described on different websites which are sometimes linked to by the sorbonne website. When you decide to take a course, you must physically find the person responsible for signing people up for the specific course. At my campus their offices were in corridors that were locked away from student access.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: None. The international/student help office specifically tell you in their emails and in person they can not help with this.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Somewhat. I managed to register for some of the courses I wanted. But I was never added to the mailing list with eg. exam information, meaning I didn't know the exam format, and just had to show up and hope for the best. Stuff like that is to be expected no matter how hard you try.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Studying at Sorbonne takes an extreme amount of will-power, not for the academics, but for the administration. You will be misinformed, sent in circles, not answered, meat deadends and everything in between simply because you wish to sign up for courses. When I answered the universitys inqueries about which courses I wished to attend, before I left for the exchange, I was personally phoned by an administrator, laughed at and ridiculed for picking "the wrong courses" and for not speaking french. I am not making this up, and I am not mad at the university, because afterall, I had a lovely exchange, I am mentioning it to warn future exchange students that you need to be able to handle a lot and not give up to power through the administrative procedures for studying at Sorbonne.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Some courses were very difficult, some more at a KU level.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More high-school like. Not a single book or pdf was to be read for my whole semester. Everything is based on showing up to the lectures, and writing down what the professor says.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Cloud computing
Statistics in Bioinformatics and Sequence Algorithms
Programming in C++
French as a foreign language

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All of them, I think they were all interesting. All students found Cloud Computing extremely difficult, with a lot of them spending several days every week on the labs, but it was a very interesting course. French as a foreign language was really nice for learning french, but beware of some of the teachers, some of them are very "old school" and will ridicule students who find the language hard. Lucky for me I wasnt among the worst, so I wasnt bullied by any of the teachers, but the same could not be said for all students.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I cant think of any.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Public transport was more expensive. Eating at the university was less expensive at 3.3 euroes per meal.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All kinds of sport, if you managed to find out about it.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I participated in the universitys brazilian jiu-jitsu class. It was awesome, 1,5 hour sports class in the middle of the day, great facility, the vibes could not have been better.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I dont know, go on trips, see the museums in Paris, hang out in the parisian bars.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: More difficult than I thought, many frenchmen will treat you like trash if you are nice to them but dont speak french. Be polite, but dont be too nice/smiling.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: The only local students who were open to talking with me were in my sports class. Otherwise, they are, understandably so, pretty set in their social circles.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The arrogance. French stereotypes hold up 100% with their arrogance and displeasantries. I learned to handle this by being polite but stern, this way they dont "smell blood" and will treat you like a frenchman.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The always going out culture is amazing.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
The administrative procedures are not for the faint of heart.
Paris is amazing and full of fun.
You can learn a lot of french through the universitys free french courses, but remember to participate actively.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Participate in the socializing events in the beginning, they are great for getting a social circle.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: How much my french improved, and how well I suddenly got along with the frenchmen.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The administrative procedures of Sorbonne.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
